claims.text: Machine learning–guided high-throughput screening can rapidly identify refractory HEA compositions.
Integrating machine learning screening with thermodynamic and kinetic simulations can identify RHEAs that are intrinsically strong, ductile, and low in weight.
The initial RHEA systems have unoptimized multi-principal-element compositions.
Machine learning algorithms such as Bayesian optimization can use simulation and limited experimental datasets to screen and refine RHEA compositions.
Simulation parameters should be calibrated against known thermodynamic data.
Precise compositional tuning induces optimized phase stability in RHEAs.
Precise compositional tuning induces microstructural homogeneity in RHEAs.
Machine learning can identify correlations among RHEA composition, simulated thermodynamic properties, and mechanical performance.
The identified correlations narrow the RHEA compositional search space to candidates with predicted superior properties.
RHEAs designed by the integrated method will have statistically significantly greater strength than conventionally designed alloys.
RHEAs designed by the integrated method will have statistically significantly greater ductility than conventionally designed alloys.
RHEAs designed by the integrated method will have statistically significantly lower weight than conventionally designed alloys.
The effectiveness of the method depends on the quality and extent of the available data and on the validity of its underlying assumptions.
The method may be less effective when simulation models omit critical physical phenomena.
It is uncertain whether machine-learning predictions will produce the expected mechanical improvements across all relevant RHEA systems.
A controlled comparison using tensile strength, strain-to-failure, density, and microstructural measurements can test the hypothesis.
